items.title: Global Phase Equivalence
items.statement: Define matrix equality up to a scalar \(\lambda U\), \( |\lambda|=1\), separately from ordinary matrix equality.

items.title: Demultiplexing a two-block unitary
items.statement: For finite-dimensional unitaries U0,U1 on H, the block unitary U0⊕U1 on C²⊗H factors as (I⊗V)(D⊕D†)(I⊗W), where V,W are unitary on H and D is diagonal unitary in an orthonormal basis.

items.title: The unitary matrix group has Cayley charts of real dimension N squared
items.statement: For each integer N≥1, U(N)={Q∈M_N(C):Q*Q=QQ*=I} is a compact smooth real manifold of dimension N². Near I it has a smooth chart from the real vector space of skew-Hermitian matrices X*=-X by X↦(I+X)(I−X)^{-1}; left translates give a finite chart cover.

items.title: Cosine sine block decomposition
items.statement: For a unitary partitioned into equal square blocks, there exist block-diagonal unitaries L=diag(L0,L1), R=diag(R0,R1) and real diagonal C,S with C²+S²=I, 0≤C,S≤I, such that U=L[[C,−S],[S,C]]R. Zero and unit singular values are permitted.

items.title: One Qubit Euler Decomposition
items.statement: For every (U\in U(2)), (U=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)) for real parameters; if \(\det U=1\), the scalar is absorbed and the (SU(2)) form remains. Prove by writing the two orthonormal columns of U, parameterizing the first unit vector by two phases and an angle, and using orthogonality to fix the second column. Barenco Lemma 4.1 supplies this proof.

items.title: Two-qubit local and Pauli interaction decomposition
items.statement: Every U∈U(4) has an exact factorization U=e^{iδ}(A⊗B)exp(i(αX⊗X+βY⊗Y+γZ⊗Z))(C⊗D) for real δ,α,β,γ and A,B,C,D∈SU(2).

items.title: Two Level Unitary
items.statement: For two distinct computational-basis labels (x,y) and (V\in U(2)), the two-level unitary acts as (V) on \(\operatorname{span}\{|x\rangle,|y\rangle\}\) and as identity on the orthogonal complement. Its definition is an exact matrix, including scalar phase.

items.title: Two Level Unitary Elimination
items.statement: Exact-arithmetic input U in U(N), N≥1, with matrix entries supporting addition, multiplication, conjugation, nonnegative square root and exact zero test. Set M=U and record an empty word. For column j=0,...,N−2 and row r=N−1,...,j+1, let a=M_(r−1,j), b=M_(r,j); if b=0 skip. Otherwise h=sqrt(|a|²+|b|²)>0, apply on rows r−1,r the Givens [[conj(a)/h,conj(b)/h],[−b/h,a/h]], update M and record the factor. Return recorded factors in reverse adjoint order followed by diagonal M. This is a finite exact-arithmetic procedure; a Cauchy name alone does not supply its zero test.

items.title: Two Level Unitary Elimination Correct
items.statement: The preceding algorithm terminates after at most (N(N-1)/2) Givens rotations plus at most (N) one-coordinate phases and its matrix product is exactly U. Proof: maintain the left-product invariant, show each Givens step zeros one entry without changing prior columns, then use orthogonality to show a triangular unitary is diagonal.

items.title: Generic CNOT Parameter Count
items.statement: For a circuit skeleton on n qubits with m CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates, prove that its parameterized image has real dimension at most \(3n+4m+1\): the initial local layer contributes at most \(3n\), each CNOT contributes at most four new parameters by the local stabilizer/coset calculation, and one scalar accounts for global phase. There are finitely many skeletons for fixed n,m, so if \(3n+4m+1<4^n=\dim U(2^n)\), their smooth images have measure zero. This yields the generic lower bound in the following theorem.

items.title: Global Phase Under Control
items.statement: For \(C(U)=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes I+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U\), \(C(\lambda U)=(P_\lambda\otimes I)C(U)\), where \(P_\lambda=\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)\). Thus an uncontrolled whole-circuit scalar does not change a measurement law, but replacing a target by a phase-congruent matrix inside a control changes a relative phase unless the control phase is restored. Prove by the two control-block matrices.

items.title: Gray-code synthesis of a multiplexed one-qubit rotation
items.statement: A target rotation about a fixed Pauli axis, with one independently specified real angle for each of the 2^k computational control strings, is exactly realizable by a Gray-code circuit using 2^k one-qubit rotations and at most 2^k CNOT gates, with no ancillas.

items.title: A controlled one-qubit unitary uses at most two CNOT gates
items.statement: For every exact U∈U(2), the controlled block C(U)=diag(I,U) is exactly implementable using at most two CNOT gates and one-qubit gates; the determinant phase of U is implemented as a phase on the control.

items.title: Every two-qubit unitary has an exact three-CNOT synthesis
items.statement: Every U∈U(4) is exactly the denotation of a circuit with at most three CNOT gates and one-qubit gates; any scalar phase is implemented explicitly as a one-qubit scalar gate.

items.title: Exact Arbitrary Unitary QSD Upper Bound
items.statement: Shende–Bullock–Markov's exact Quantum Shannon Decomposition gives a no-ancilla (n)-qubit unitary circuit with at most \( (23/48)4^n-(3/2)2^n+4/3\) CNOTs, plus one-qubit gates. Their construction uses cosine-sine decomposition, multiplexors, and cancellations. This is a gate-count upper bound, not a bound on numerical decomposition time. The displayed bound applies for n≥2; n=0 requires no CNOT and n=1 requires zero CNOT. Prove the QSD CNOT recurrence and small-n base optimizations, not just existence of a decomposition.

items.title: Generic Unitary CNOT Lower Bound
items.statement: For almost every n-qubit unitary, at least \(\left\lceil(4^n-3n-1)/4\right\rceil\) CNOTs are needed in an exact no-ancilla circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates. The statement is generic and follows from the preceding parameter-count lemma.

items.title: Multicontrolled Ancilla Resource Tradeoff
items.statement: For m≥1 controls and exact U in U(2), Barenco gives a chosen no-workspace construction with O(m²) one-qubit/CNOT gates and a chosen one-clean-work-bit construction with O(m) such gates, returning that bit to zero. These are upper bounds; the source has only an Omega(m) lower bound for nonscalar U. Its explicit quadratic construction has Theta(m²) size, which is not a quadratic optimality theorem.

items.title: Two Level Gate To Elementary Gates
items.statement: Input ordered distinct n-bit x,y and exact V in U(2), n≥1. Form the Gray path g0=x,...,gd=y by flipping differing positions in increasing order. For j=0,...,d−2 swap g_j,g_(j+1) using X on the changing bit controlled on all other bits matching their common pattern. The resulting permutation P sends x to g_(d−1) and fixes y. Apply V on the final differing bit controlled on their common other bits, reordering its two basis entries if the bit in g_(d−1) is 1. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multicontrol using the declared QC11 construction with either no work or one clean bit; emit negative controls as X conjugations.

items.title: Two Level Gate Synthesis Correct
items.statement: The Gray-path construction exactly realizes the two-level matrix, with no unintended action on other basis states. State its gate/work-bit count for each chosen controlled-U implementation.

title: Continuous-Gate Universality and Exact Synthesis — Examples

items.title: Two-level rotation as an exact unitary factor
items.statement: Embed a real planar rotation [[cos θ,−sin θ],[sin θ,cos θ]] into two computational basis states and use its Euler factorization; all other basis vectors are fixed.
